findings.english_quote: The masculine genitive φρονίμου agrees with θεοῦ, describing God as wise, while μεγάλης agrees with χειρός and describes the hand as great.
findings.issue: The note incorrectly treats φρονίμου as exclusively masculine. φρόνιμος is a two-termination adjective, and φρονίμου can qualify either masculine θεοῦ or feminine χειρός. The main rendering, “the great hand of the wise God,” is grammatically defensible, but the material alternative, “the great, wise hand of God,” is not disclosed. The following description of the hand's creative activity supports considering the latter attachment.
findings.suggested_revision: Replace the morphological claim with an accurate ambiguity note: “φρονίμου can qualify either God or the hand. The main text attaches it to θεοῦ, yielding ‘the great hand of the wise God.’ Alternatively, attaching it to χειρός gives ‘the great, wise hand of God,’ which fits the following description of the hand's activity.” Explicitly compare these readings before deciding whether to retain the main wording.

findings.source_quote: ἔτι τε ὀρέων πλήθη καὶ ὕψη, λίθων διαφοράς, μυχοὺς φοβερούς, πηγάς, ποταμούς, λίμνας, θαλάσσας, λιμένας, νήσους, ὕλας, οἰκουμένην τε πᾶσαν καὶ ἀοικήτους τόπους.
findings.english_quote: There are also the numbers and heights of mountains, the differences among stones, fearsome recesses, springs, rivers, lakes, seas, harbors, islands, forests, the whole inhabited world, and uninhabited places.
findings.issue: Every catalogue item is represented, but the supplied existential sentence conceals the Greek construction. The explicitly accusative items, beginning with διαφοράς, naturally continue or elliptically resume the objects of εἰπεῖν in the preceding sentence. The draft resets the catalogue as a statement of existence without preserving or explaining its connection to what cannot be described. The printed full stop does not require treating the accusatives as corruption.
findings.suggested_revision: Preserve the elliptical catalogue rather than supplying an independent existential assertion, for example: “And further: the multitudes and heights of mountains, varieties of stones, fearsome recesses, springs, rivers, lakes, seas, harbors, islands, forests, the whole inhabited world, and uninhabited places.” Add a source-quoted note explaining that the accusatives naturally continue the catalogue governed by εἰπεῖν across the edition's full stop, extending the preceding inability to describe these things. This is interpretation of surviving syntax, not restoration of missing text.
